I reviewed the redlines Anna referenced (procurement pointer received). High-level legal stance and proposed language:

1) Roles — we can accept 'Processor' language for Redwood; however, we need to preserve the ability to route requests to compatible model variants and to run within our dedicated infra. Proposed change: replace the customer's 'exclusive-processor' phrasing with a scoped processor obligation that preserves routing fallbacks (see proposed clause: 'Processor shall retain responsibility for execution of Requests but may route or fallback to compatible model variants and infrastructure to meet availability requirements, provided Controller data is handled per this DPA').

2) Export obligations — we can support on-demand SFTP export (push) as an operational deliverable, but cannot guarantee retention formats beyond the standard export CSV/JSON spec. We will provide the runbook and export schema. If customer needs a persistent archival SLA, that should be in Order Form (Addendum: Export Retention).

3) SCCs / Transfers — we can sign standard SCCs. Any carveouts (e.g., prohibitions on subprocessor usage in specific jurisdictions) will need a written exception path with an exec-level signoff.

I attached a short diff with proposed redlines (attachment: orderform-diff.docx). Laura — please prepare the SCCs mapping PDF and list of completed attestations. Irene — once we have the evidence bundle, we should schedule a 30-min call with Novus counsel.

—Ben
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

• Export files in newline-delimited JSON or CSV with a manifest file that includes a SHA256 checksum.
• Signed SCCs summary and a snapshot of subprocessor list stamped with date.

Procurement preference is to get the evidence bundle by close of business Monday (2026-07-06 CET) so legal can fold it into the redline review. If Redwood can move faster on the export runbook + subprocessor snapshot we can avoid a separate evidence call.

Attaching the counsel redline PDF (attachment: novus_dpa_redlines.pdf).
